<reason>CON won a competitive debate by making the voting issue easier: the duty either duplicates already-criminal threats/doxxing at the core or prices still-lawful swarms as foreseeable harm after injury, so over-removal remains the rational response. PRO had the cleaner tort framing (distinct actor, complementary interruption, bounded precautions) and stayed format-disciplined, but never fully escaped hindsight or showed why a litigable “when warranted” harbor beats throttling.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON’s Rebuttal 2: PRO’s live-location example collapses into stalking or ordinary protest, and a post-injury harbor still leaves “credible/proportionate/when warranted” litigable—so vanishing the swarm stays cheaper than proving reasonableness.</best_rebuttal>
